docs.title: Sleep paralysis at awakening: what REM atonia can explain
docs.h1: Sleep paralysis at awakening: what REM atonia can explain
docs.summary: Sleep paralysis can occur when awareness returns while REM-related muscle atonia briefly persists. Learn what the experience can and cannot tell you.
docs.blurb: Sleep paralysis can occur when awareness returns while REM-related muscle atonia briefly persists. Learn what the experience can and cannot tell you.
markers: Whether voluntary movement was temporarily impossible
Approximate duration of immobility
Whether unusual visual, auditory, or sensed-presence experiences occurred
Whether breathing felt difficult even though respiration continued
Whether the episode occurred while falling asleep or waking

docs.title: Hypnic jerks at sleep onset: sudden body jolts during the transition to sleep
docs.h1: Hypnic jerks at sleep onset: sudden body jolts during the transition to sleep
docs.summary: Hypnic jerks are brief involuntary movements around sleep onset and are usually benign. Falling sensations or a sudden jolt do not identify a precise brain mechanism.
docs.blurb: Hypnic jerks are brief involuntary movements around sleep onset and are usually benign. Falling sensations or a sudden jolt do not identify a precise brain mechanism.
markers: Whether the movement was a single jerk or repeated series
Which part of the body moved
Whether a falling or startle sensation accompanied it
Whether the event immediately caused full awakening
Whether episodes are occasional or frequent

docs.title: Racing heartbeat at sleep onset: what a hypnagogic palpitation can and cannot show
docs.h1: Racing heartbeat at sleep onset: what a hypnagogic palpitation can and cannot show
docs.summary: Heart rate and autonomic activity change across the wake-to-sleep transition, but a racing-heart sensation does not identify N1, a neurotransmitter surge, or an arrhythmia.
docs.blurb: Heart rate and autonomic activity change across the wake-to-sleep transition, but a racing-heart sensation does not identify N1, a neurotransmitter surge, or an arrhythmia.
markers: Approximate duration of the racing-heart sensation
Whether the rhythm feels regular or irregular
Whether dizziness, faintness, chest pain, or shortness of breath occurs
Whether stimulants, medications, or recent sleep loss may be relevant context
How frequently the event recurs

docs.title: REM sleep without atonia: RSWA, movement during REM, and the RBD distinction
docs.h1: REM sleep without atonia: RSWA, movement during REM, and the RBD distinction
docs.summary: REM sleep without atonia is an objective EMG finding during REM sleep. RSWA alone is not the same as REM sleep behavior disorder.
docs.blurb: REM sleep without atonia is an objective EMG finding during REM sleep. RSWA alone is not the same as REM sleep behavior disorder.
markers: Whether movements are small isolated twitches or complex dream-enactment behaviors
Whether punching, kicking, grabbing, or leaving the bed occurs
Whether vocalizations accompany the movements
Whether the person or bed partner has been injured
Whether behavior is recurrent

docs.title: Sleep bruxism: jaw-muscle activity during sleep
docs.h1: Sleep bruxism: jaw-muscle activity during sleep
docs.summary: Sleep bruxism is rhythmic or non-rhythmic masticatory muscle activity during sleep. Jaw soreness or tooth wear alone cannot determine its sleep stage or cause.
docs.blurb: Sleep bruxism is rhythmic or non-rhythmic masticatory muscle activity during sleep. Jaw soreness or tooth wear alone cannot determine its sleep stage or cause.
markers: Whether grinding sounds are reported during sleep
Morning jaw-muscle fatigue, pain, or stiffness
Tooth wear, fractures, or dental damage
How frequently the behavior is noticed
Whether snoring or other sleep symptoms coexist

docs.title: Body sensations while waking: the hypnopompic transition
docs.h1: Body sensations while waking: the hypnopompic transition
docs.summary: Brief jolts, unusual body sensations, or autonomic changes can occur while waking. The sensation alone does not prove REM, residual atonia, or a specific neural mechanism.
docs.blurb: Brief jolts, unusual body sensations, or autonomic changes can occur while waking. The sensation alone does not prove REM, residual atonia, or a specific neural mechanism.
markers: The exact body sensation noticed during awakening
Approximate duration
Whether normal voluntary movement returned immediately
Whether palpitations or breathing difficulty occurred
Whether episodes recur and disrupt sleep

docs.title: Periodic limb movements during sleep: PLMS, repeated leg movements, and PLMD
docs.h1: Periodic limb movements during sleep: PLMS, repeated leg movements, and PLMD
docs.summary: PLMS are repetitive stereotyped limb movements measured during sleep. Their clinical significance varies, and one remembered kick does not diagnose PLMS or PLMD.
docs.blurb: PLMS are repetitive stereotyped limb movements measured during sleep. Their clinical significance varies, and one remembered kick does not diagnose PLMS or PLMD.
markers: Whether movements appear repetitive and stereotyped rather than isolated
Whether a bed partner notices recurring leg or foot movements
Whether movements appear to disrupt sleep
Whether restless-leg sensations occur while awake before sleep
Whether there is meaningful daytime sleepiness or fatigue

docs.title: Breathing pauses at sleep onset: transition physiology versus sleep apnea
docs.h1: Breathing pauses at sleep onset: transition physiology versus sleep apnea
docs.summary: Breathing control changes as wakefulness gives way to sleep, and brief central pauses can occur near sleep onset. A felt pause or gasp cannot diagnose sleep apnea.
docs.blurb: Breathing control changes as wakefulness gives way to sleep, and brief central pauses can occur near sleep onset. A felt pause or gasp cannot diagnose sleep apnea.
markers: Whether another person has witnessed repeated breathing pauses
Whether there is recurrent gasping or choking during sleep
Whether loud habitual snoring is present
Whether excessive daytime sleepiness is present
Whether the event is isolated or repeatedly disrupts sleep

docs.title: Confusional arousal: incomplete awakening from NREM sleep
docs.h1: Confusional arousal: incomplete awakening from NREM sleep
docs.summary: Confusional arousals are disorders of arousal involving incomplete awakening from NREM sleep with confusion or disoriented behavior.
docs.blurb: Confusional arousals are disorders of arousal involving incomplete awakening from NREM sleep with confusion or disoriented behavior.
markers: Approximate duration of confusion after the apparent awakening
Whether speech or behavior was disorganized
How much of the event was remembered afterward
Whether complex behaviors such as walking occurred
Whether the event created a risk of injury

docs.title: Exploding head syndrome: a sudden sound sensation at the sleep–wake boundary
docs.h1: Exploding head syndrome: a sudden sound sensation at the sleep–wake boundary
docs.summary: Exploding head syndrome involves a sudden perceived bang or explosive sound around a sleep transition. Its underlying mechanism remains uncertain.
docs.blurb: Exploding head syndrome involves a sudden perceived bang or explosive sound around a sleep transition. Its underlying mechanism remains uncertain.
markers: What the perceived sound or sensory burst was like
Whether there was any matching external sound
Whether the event occurred while falling asleep or waking
Whether pain, weakness, confusion, or other neurological symptoms occurred
How often the episodes recur

docs.title: Fragmented REM sleep: repeated arousals, awakenings, and what they can show
docs.h1: Fragmented REM sleep: repeated arousals, awakenings, and what they can show
docs.summary: REM sleep can be interrupted by arousals and awakenings. Subjective broken sleep or fragmented dream recall cannot by itself prove REM fragmentation.
docs.blurb: REM sleep can be interrupted by arousals and awakenings. Subjective broken sleep or fragmented dream recall cannot by itself prove REM fragmentation.

Whether dream recall appears as several separate fragments
